body_en_plain:
March, 1992       Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 H. A. Thatcher.......03    04

 D.E. Ottery..........07    11

 John Hunter..........14    18

 Frank Lambert........19    26

 Alan D. Cox..........32    45

 C.W.G. Coppin........52    54

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: H.A. Thatcher, LONDON


Having changed from +3 to SAM, I
am finding that most PD people
are using 64 columns.

As I use a 14" TV there is a
shimmering or flicker on text in
colour and graphics. Some of
your programs I cannot read.

Have you a solution? It is not
the tuning as the programs on my
+3 are not affected.

             Yours,

          H.A. Thatcher

Brian Cavers to H.A. Thatcher

Yes, there is an obsession with
64 and 80-column isn't there? I
prefer to use whatever is appro-
priate to the job whether 32, 64
or 80. No one format is "better"
than another; newspapers have
used narrow columns for years
because it is easier to see(eyes
tend to find it hard to locate
the start of the next line when
they have been focussed on the
end of the preceding line, 80
character away to the right!

Anyway -  to your problem of the
dreaded shimmers, you could open
the power supply unit and adjust
the tv output. It has three tiny
screws you can experiment with..

Take one screw at a time and
give it a half turn to see the
effect on the display. Give it
further half turns, counting as
you go, and turn it back as it
was at the start if you do not
improve the display. Now try it
in the opposite direction. Try
the other screws if you are not
successful. I recollect that one
of the screws helps with the
sound. Only do the foregoing if
you feel confident about opening
electrical components and tink-
ering with them. There is a live
connection to the transformer
which is dangerous and one of
the screws is quite fragile (it
is ceramic I think) and can
break. I can't accept any
responsibility for damage etc.

If you have no success then you
probably have a faulty SAM and
may wish to return it for repair
to PBT. The only alternative is
to buy a monitor instead. The
Philips CMB833 seems popular.

One last thing - if you are
"sharing" the tv with the +3 via
an aerial splitter then, if the
+3 and SAM are outputting on
very close frequencies (as they
often may be)then you may suffer
display problems because they
interfere with each other. If
you disconnect the +3 you will
soon see if this is the problem.
If so, adjust your SAM's PSU TV
output as described above or
keep the +3 disconnected while
using the SAM.         - Brian

From: D.E. Ottery, SOMERSET

Dear Ron and Brian

I have just finished reading
through OUTLET 53 and have
noticed several things that I
thought required comment.

1) The new version of OUTWRITE!
sounds good. Will the maximum
file length be increased? Will
there be an 80-column mode?
(Please). Will it use MASTERDOS
to the full and include sub-
directories?

If this is so, I'll certainly
upgrade and no doubt you'll
inform everyone through OUTLET
when the upgrade is available.

2) The IQ test featured in this
Issue was also on FRED Issue 10.

3) With reference to the letter
about transfer of files to the
PC via 3.5" disc, the suite of
programs you refer to in the SDC
Supplement are in Issue 7 and
include a program to send text
files either way, as well as a
program that allows you to type
SAM BASIC programs on a PC as an
ASCII file, (e.g. from a text
editor or wordprocessor).It then
converts the ASCII into BASIC.

The programs are a bit "rough
and ready"though but SD Software
(70,Rainhall Road, Barnoldswick,
Lancs BB8 6AB)sell a compilation
of programs called "PC-Suite".

"PC-Suite" is by the same author
(Ian Spencer) and are basically
the same programs [as those in
SAM Supplement] but linked
together better through menus.

The pack transfers text files
from WORDMASTER as, like many PC
WPs, it ends each line with a
carriage return,unlike TASWORD 2
and OUTWRITE! which fill up the
line with spaces.

A program is included allowing
you to format 720K PC discs on
SAM.The pack works fine for what
I want to do with it,which is to
program in Modula-2 using OUT-
WRITE! and to transfer file to
PCs at the university. Since it
copes with this,I'm sure it will
cope with "normal" text.

The program costs a vast `25.95
(`19.95 to INDUG members -
(remember your number!) and
comes with a concise but useful
manual. Please also add p&p at
50p (`1.20 outside U.K.)

             Yours,

           D.E. Ottery

Brian Cavers to D.E. Ottery

1) The new upgrade version of
OUTWRITE will have the same file
length and 64-column screen.This
is fixed by the original code
and cannot be changed without a
massive re-write which cannot be
justified commercially by a
budget wordprocessor. The latest
prototype I have of OUTWRITE is,
within the constraints of its
type - i.e., simple-to-use, very
low-priced wordprocessor aimed
at the average home user -one of
the most perfected and polished
pieces of software I have seen.
It WILL be able to access sub-
directories under MASTERDOS and
it CAN also print one document
while you type another under
MASTERBASIC.

2)You can expect to see software
in different disc magazines just
as the same book is in various
libraries.It's only on the SAM
such a point would be raised -it
is the norm on'normal'computers.

If you send a program to OUTLET
we do not claim your copyright -
it is YOURS. If you want to send
it elsewhere - you can - whether
PD or not. Only if you have an
agreement to give exclusive
rights to a publisher should you
not send it elsewhere. It may be
in writing or as an announcement
in a magazine,e.g.,"any software
contributed to our magazine will
become our copyright". Even this
could be challenged by an author
subsequently so a written agree-
ment is best.

Thanks for the PC-SUITE info. It
is probably about the right
price in such a small market and
emphasises the very high value
of disc magazines when they
include such software(or almost)
for a fraction of the price.
People just don't realize the
hard work involved or the small
returns from such a tiny market.

Modula-2 in OUTWRITE eh?There is
a Spectrum version of Modula-2
now. If you have a Spectrum and
I can scrounge a review copy,
perhaps you would be willing to
review it for us?

                        - Brian

From John Hunter, MID-GLAMORGAN

  CALCULATION OF EASTER SUNDAY

I have a formula which will
calculate on what day Easter
Sunday will fall, but only for
the years 1753 onwards. As you
will possibly know, in September
1752 the calendar changed from
Julian to Gregorian by omitting
11 days i.e.
        SEPTEMBER  1752

      SUN         17    24
      MON         18    25
      TUE   1     19    26
      WED   2     20    27
      THU  14     21    28
      FRI  15     22    29
      SAT  16     23    30

My program for Easter Sundays
(only valid for 1753 onwards)is:

940  LPRINT "Easter Sundays":
LPRINT:LPRINT:LPRINT

945 INPUT "1st year ? ";Z, "Last
year ? ";Q

950 LET Y=INT (Z/19): LET A=Z-
(Y*19) : LET B=INT (Z/100): LET
C=Z-(100+B):LET D=INT (B/4): LET
E=B-(4*D):LET G=INT((8*B+13)/25)

955 LET T=19*A+B-D-G+15: LET
X=INT (T/30): LET H=T-30*X: LET
J=INT ((A+11*H)/319): LET M=INT
(C/4): LET K=C-4*M

960 LET S=2*E+2*M-K-H+J+32: LET
W=INT (S/7): LET R=S-7*W: LET
N=INT ((H-J+R+90)/25)

965 LET U=H-J+R+N+19: LET V=INT
(U/32): LET P=U-32*V

967 IF P<10 then let QQ=0: GOTO
973

970 LPRINT P;"/";N;"/";Z: LET
Z=Z+1: IF Z>Q THEN GOTO 980

972 IF Z<=Q THEN GOTO 975

973 LPRINT QQ;P;"/";N;"/";Z: LET
Z=Z+1: IF Z>Q THEN GOTO 980

975 GOTO 950

980 LPRINT "End of run. ":
LPRINT:LPRINT

      ====================

I have included this program in
case anyone is interested and
can possibly add an amendment
that would cover the years prior
to 1753.

Possibly  E. Thomson might have
an interest as he produced
"KWICAL" for OUTLET which gave
the Calendar program to cover
pre-1753 as well as current
calendar dates.

        Yours sincerely,

            J. HUNTER

Brian Cavers to John Hunter

Mmmmmm. What happens if you just
subtract 14 days from the result
if the year is earlier than 1753
to give the Sunday two weeks
before? It occurs to me that,
without an early calendar, it
would be difficult to test one's
results. Incidentally as this is
not a paper magazine, one of the
advantages is that you can send
in, and I can publish, the
original program. This would
save anyone interested typing in
your program all over again and
also avoid any errors. Printed
listings are notoriously unreli-
able as a single character out
of place may make the program
unworkable.
                          Brian

From: Frank Lambert, HORNCHURCH

I've not written since receiving
"OUTWRITE" with comments about
the program. Although I've kept
an eye on the letters column and
the various replies you've made.

1) Firstly, I use a Canon
PV-1080A printer and there are
some differences in control
codes from those used in
'OUTWRITE. Also I require 'back-
space' facilities so I've re-
written the 2nd Help Page to my
own requirements.

2) I also prefer not to have a
space sent with each control
code - so all 32's have been
deleted by repoking where
necessary.

This, of course, makes permanent
the advice you gave to overcome
start of paragraph indentation.
However, it has to be remem-
bered, and this applies to your
advice as well,that right margin
justification is upset.

3)I have to say that the problem
of lack of right justification
after the introduction of
control codes is a fault, al-
though I suspect to correct it
would entail a great deal of
work. Indeed it was a fault in
most of the SPECTRUM word
processor programs. In my
experience only "The Last Word"
was fault free in this respect
and I feel it is a pity that
'OUTWRITE' doesn't measure up in
this respect.

4)I found the lack of a flashing
cursor annoying as I frequently
managed to lose it.


However, your suggestion of a
cure by use of a coloured cursor
is brilliant. I introduced a red
cursor and have had no problems
at all since - incidentally I
had no difficulty in following
your instructions.


5) Now something of a 'tongue in
cheek' comment. I think your
criticism of Mike Haine's
"delete" criticism is a litle
unfortunate, as the program uses
"delete" with two different
meanings.

In the case of a symbol, it has
the meaning replace "symbol" by
"space" - but in the case of a
line, "delete" means "remove
line in its entirety" - and not
"replace line by a line of
spaces"! These usages may follow
"usual custom" which is really
the basis of your criticism of
Mike Haine's comment, but
repetition of 'common' error is
no basis for valid criticism!

Now, a word on FREEWARE and P.D.
SOFTWARE which has implication
for programs like "OUTWRITE".

You have commented that extended
programs offering facilities
that only few might use could
only be marketed at greatly
increased, (uneconomic?) prices.

I suggest that the introduction
of FREEWARE and P.D. SOFTWARE
makes it necessary to grasp that
particular nettle - since their
introduction has gone too far to
stop, even if it were wanted -
and there is at least one prog-
ram, for all practical purposes
as good as "OUTWRITE" available
as FREEWARE.


This can only mean that there
are enough programmers 'out
there' to supply reasonable
programs just for the fun of it.
It also implies that 'programs
for sale' have to be the
extensive programs requiring a
team of programmers employed by
a software house.

That further implies that those
of us who wish to acquire such
programs will have to pay an
economic market price. This, of
course, only applies to
'serious' programs.

'Games' i.e. the saleable ones,
already require a team to
produce them, but the market
volume is sufficient to keep the
price to a reasonable level.


The only other way would be for
the software houses to subsidise
the serious programs from the
profits of the games programs
c.f. the claims always made that
"pop" records subsidise
"classical".

After all the doom and gloom,
may I offer you both a belated
happy New Year - and keep up the
good work. I am still amazed
that you continue to further
improve the magazine - I am
unable to comprehend how you
manage to do it.

        Yours sincerely,

          Frank Lambert

Brian Cavers to Frank Lambert

I wonder if you'd mind sending
your text file next time, Frank?
It does help us enormously and
is much appreciated. It seems a
waste for you to type it all in,
print it, send it to us - then
we have to type it all in again!
It's a bit of a slog, especially
with a big letter. I know we do
say we accept letters in any
form but we also add, "please
send your textfile!". A disc can
be sent at no extra postage and
we do return all discs. Thanks!

2+3) You remove the very spaces
which replace codes to retain
justification then complain that
the lack of justification is a
"fault"!

No,that is not a fault; the only
"fault" is simply the limitation
that one could only insert one
code in one space.To some extent
this has been overcome in the
new upgrade version as each code
now contains up to 20 characters
and there will be an additional
10 "user-defined" (although ALL
the codes may be redefined by
the user). Also, the method of
changing the codes sent has been
improved dramatically and become
so easy and clear that you can
rapidly set up several "printer
drivers" to suit if you wanted.
I agree being able to define say
BOLD ITALICS in one on-screen
code is O.K. but not so flexible
as entering them separately in
one "position".

However,many users will often
use the same groupings of codes
so this is a great improvement.


5) I think your criticism of my
criticism of Mike Haine's
criticism is wrong and I reject
it utterly. If you read my
comments again you will see that
I make it quite clear that if
method A is preferred of two
methods: A and B, it does not
follow that B is wrong.

Furthermore, I make it clear in
absolute terms that I think both
methods are acceptable, are not
erroneous but that OUTWRITE uses
just one method and not the
other.

It is a mistake to think that
the method used is "common"error
which has been followed blindly;
that method has been chosen by
preference. I repeat:

IT IS NOT A "WRONG" METHOD,IT IS
NOT A FAULT; IT IS NOT AN ERROR.

Your criticism is liking saying
black ink on white is a common
error whereas the correct way is
to have white on black!

I hear no reasoned, logical
arguments explaining why one
method is correct and the other
wrong; I only hear an assumption
based on personal preference and
I will not accept such criticism
without a fight!

Regarding the wordprocessor that
is in the public domain, please
send it in to us and I will put
it in OUTLET so we can ask other
readers for their opinion.I take
it you are not speaking of a
word processor on some other
computer such as a PC? Indeed,as
far as price goes, some PD discs
on other systems costs several
pounds and the `12 of OUTWRITE
might be regarded as a PD price
on some machines. I remember a
PC owner at an ALL-FORMATS FAIR
being very impressed with
OUTWRITE on screen and assumed
it to be public domain when he
saw the price. He was very dis-
appointed when I explained it
was not available for his PC and
he had to go back to struggling
with his over-complex WP!

Do not take anything personal in
the previous outburst! As stated
before, when attacked I will
defend wholeheartedly because I
cannot accept the possibility of
others being mislead.

                        - Brian.

From: Alan D. Cox,
      Pen-y-Maes, Ostrey Hill,
      St.Clears, Dyfed, SA33 4AJ

Dear Ron and Brian,

First, at the risk of being a
bore, may I again comment that I
cannot see how SCPDSA can say
they are dealing in PD software
and at the same time claim copy-
right in their material - it
really is a nonsense.

I note that despite the
opportunity offered by earlier
correspondence, including a
letter of mine, Mr. Stevens has
not attempted to justify his
erroneous description of the
material he is selling.

I found ALPHAKEY a useful item,
if only because it gives the
items in alphabetical order.

However, I think it a pity that
John McCabe did not give the
'full' codes for all the key-
words etc: specifically, he
ignores the fact that for some
of the items i.e. those given on
page 65 of the Technical Manual,
the correct code is FFh followed
by the appropriate number.  The
full code for SCREEN$ is 255 76.

This can be easily seen by
writing a small BASIC program
and then PEEKing the area in
which it is stored (at DPEEK
&5AA0 + &4000 - not &8000 as
stated in the Technical Manual)

I was interested to see RAND-
SCRAPER - I remember this prog-
ram from my Spectrum days, and I
thought I had a copy but cannot
find it - was it in an early
OUTLET?. It has been extensively
reworked for SAM and is well
worth republishing.

In Stephen Wilson's SAMCLASS he
equates Hertz to cycles in one
place - it should surely be
cycles per second (sorry, but I
get more pedantic as I grow
older!) Whilst on the point of
old age, I hope you will forgive
me for saying that some of your
more exotic opening screens for
items are, for my poor old eyes,
very difficult to read - an
example this month is 4 Square,

with blocked letters in italics
and with a shadow - and no, it
is not my screen, which is
better than average in my
opinion (I originally typed
'view', but thought the pun un-
fortunate!). It is only a minor
moan, but if no-one tells you,
you won't know of our problems!

I was interested to see SHRINK,
which appears to be a SAM
version of the classic pseudo-AI
program called ELIZA. If your
readers are interested in this
subject they may like to look at
Mike James' article in the
February 1992 issue of Computer
Shopper, entitled 'All in the
mind' - and there are related
articles in earlier Shoppers.

Having raised the question of
copyright earlier in this
letter, I have a problem in this
area myself.   One of my sins -
I'm not going to tell you the
others! - is that I occasionally
dabble with my Wife's AMSTRAD
PCW 8256, and I also read 8000+
(now called PCW PLUS).

In the November 1991 issue there
was an interesting short Mallard
BASIC program to print out bar-
codes given an input of the bar-
code number. Out of interest,
and also because the author's
name happened to be Alan Dennis
(which are my Christian names) I
decided to convert this to a SAM
program (not difficult, but not
trivial either.

I appreciated the Spectrum/SAM
string-slicing commands more and
more as I struggled with the
Mallard equivalents).

Once this was working, I thought
it might be of some interest to
other Spectrum/SAM users, so I
wrote to the Editor of 8000+
asking if she would object if my
version was published in OUTLET
(i.e. if you were interested).

However, 8000+ operate a policy
of only replying to letters if
they can do so in their letters
columns (which may be a reason-
able policy for general letters,
although I believe they would
please their readers more if
they were more responsive in

this area - and yes, I remember
your comments on reacting to
readers queries, although I
think you are wrong), but I felt
a query such as mine deserved a
reply by letter, particularly
since I had said I would fully
acknowledge their copyright.
However, as you can deduce I
have had no response.

So where do I stand? If you
think the program is of any
interest, would you be prepared
to publish it, with full
recognition of 8000+ and the
original author's copyright?

Or do you feel that the refusal
of 8000+ to respond must be
taken as refusal of the right to
copy?

(I should say that I have not
altered the essential ideas in
the program, although the
Spectrum/SAM conversions are my
own work).

As a light aside, I do not know
how many of your readers are
superstitious but I wonder how
many of those who are know that
the 13th of a month is more
likely to be a Friday than any
other day of the week? I came
across this fact many years ago
in Rouse Ball's Mathematical
Recreations and Essays, and
verified it by hand. It is an
interesting exercise in calendar
calculations to check it out on
Spectrum/SAM - the key is to
remember the 400 year calendar
cycle.

For those who may be concerned,
the relative proportions of
different days of the week are
only just biased in favour of
Friday.

Apropos versions of BASIC. Over
Christmas I had the opportunity
to play with my younger Son's
ATARI 520STFM. He uses it for
word processing and games, and
has never seriously tried the
BASIC supplied with the machine.
I did - and it's APPALLING!

Say what you will about Clive
Sinclair, he provided a splendid
BASIC (which of course has
influenced SAM's BASIC as well).
Indeed, it might be argued that
as well as encouraging the


growth of the hobby computer
scene with his succession of
excellent and affordable
machines. The user-friendly
nature of ZX80/81 and Spectrum
BASIC also made a major
contribution. If I had had to
struggle with ATARI BASIC early
on I might well have become
totally disillusioned.

I note what you say in response
to my comments on SAMCo's News-
disk. I didn't expect you to
agree with me!

However, if what you say about
SAMCo using the Newsdisk as a
medium for publishing a dis-
assembly of the SAM ROM is true
then things becomes even more
ludicrous.

I don't expect to find serious
technical material such as this
in the midst of what is being
offered as a collection of
playable demos (presumably
mainly of games, in which I have
no real interest), news (i.e.
advertisements) of SAM related
products and gossip.

I hope that I shall not be
denied the opportunity to get a
disassembly of SAM's ROM just
because I refuse to pay for what
ought to be free advertising
material.

Incidentally, as I said, I wrote
to Alan Miles on this matter,
but as yet I have not received
the courtesy of either an
acknowledgement or a reply.

And please do not tell me about
the problem of firms replying to
letters - by and large firms
need customers more than
customers need firms, and even
if the firm believes that the
customer is not always right,
they should at least respond to
criticisms.

As I said earlier, whatever the
costs, a sensible firm ought to
budget for dealing with letters
in order to keep serious
customers happy.

Finally, I recently acquired,
through the pages of Micro
Computer Mart, a Tandy Colour
Graphics Printer CGP 115, which
is a super little machine.

I'd be grateful to learn whether
any of your readers can help me
with a couple of problems - one
with the DIP switches and one
with the CHR$(19) command. I am
happy for you to publish my
address in case anyone wants to
write to me directly.

As ever, all best wishes, and
congratulations on a super
'magazine'

         Alan Dennis Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

I think SCPDSA's claim to copy-
right referred to their first
disc in response to being asked
why they corrupted the directory
to prevent people copying the
files. I don't know what other
claims to copyright they make or
if they have changed their pos-
tion because it is simply not
clear whether their material IS
genuinely in the public domain
or not.

Not all of the material in their
catalogue is marked as "PD" and
nowhere is "PD" defined.There is
no declaration that "public
domain" means anyone can copy it
or sell it for a nominal cost as
on other computers.

Nor is any of the software that
I have seen marked as public
domain or "FREEWARE" as we do.

The catalogue's front cover has
the sub-heading "The Complete
Guide to Public Domain Software
For the SAM Coupe" which is
obviously not true since they do
not include any OUTLET material.

All-in-all, my feeling is that
the originators used the label
"PD" without knowing what it
really means but have just heard
it and thought it a "trendy"
expression to use.

Not all the material is in the
public domain because I have
asked individuals.

I agree that they should either
declare all or part of the mat-
erial genuinely in the public
domain and announce that it may
be freely copied or re-sold so
long as only a modest charge is
made to cover costs (this cost
MAY include labour costs as is
the general practice with PD
libraries on other computers) or
they should remove the term "PD"
from their name.

Again,the rights of contributing
authors is paramount. Anyone
writing software and wishing it
to be in the public domain MUST
be reassured that it will be
treated as such and is free to
be copied by anyone and dispers-
ed as widely as possible.

Regarding your comment on copy-
right, I must say that it IS
normal for an author to declare
his work "in the public domain"
and yet retain the copyright but
this is a technicality and is
really just to make clear who
the author really is or perhaps
simply to stop anyone blatantly
taking a PD program, dressing it
up, packaging it and promoting
it as their own software.It does
NOT mean the software must not
be copied etc or that the author
has any further control such as
cancelling the PD status!

Note PD means both"software free
of copy restrictions" AND the
blanket term for LICENCEWARE,
SHAREWARE etc. where copyright
IS crucial.

Again, with PD, it is as if one
retains the copyright but allows
the public free licence to copy
it. In any event, that is the
way it is - even if it is hard
to understand. What doesn't make
sense is declaring something PD
and then saying nobody must copy
it and even protecting it from
being copied! This is nonsense.

I agree the 4 Square title was
very hard to read but I didn't
do it! The author himself used
my TEXAT routine (it's PD!) and
I am loathe to change something
of that nature in someone's own
software. I remove bugs, correct
spelling and grammar, I may even
add improvements (I add a front
title page if there isn't one).

However, I try to leave alone

Yes, there is an obsession with 64 and 80-column isn't there? I prefer to use whatever is appro- priate to the job whether 32, 64 or 80. Anyway -  to your problem of the dreaded shimmers, you could open the power supply unit and adjust the tv output. It has three tiny screws you can experiment with..

Take one screw at a time and give it a half turn to see the effect on the display. Give it further half turns, counting as you go, and turn it back as it was at the start if you do not improve the display. Now try it in the opposite direction. Try the other screws if you are not successful. I recollect that one of the screws helps with the sound. Only do the foregoing if you feel confident about opening electrical components and tink- ering with them. There is a live connection to the transformer which is dangerous and one of the screws is quite fragile (it is ceramic I think) and can break. I can't accept any responsibility for damage etc.

If you have no success then you probably have a faulty SAM and may wish to return it for repair to PBT. The only alternative is to buy a monitor instead. The Philips CMB833 seems popular.

One last thing - if you are "sharing" the tv with the +3 via an aerial splitter then, if the +3 and SAM are outputting on very close frequencies (as they often may be)then you may suffer display problems because they interfere with each other. From: Frank Lambert, HORNCHURCH

I've not written since receiving "OUTWRITE" with comments about the program. Although I've kept an eye on the letters column and the various replies you've made.

1) Firstly, I use a Canon PV-1080A printer and there are some differences in control codes from those used in 'OUTWRITE. Also I require 'back- space' facilities so I've re- written the 2nd Help Page to my own requirements.

2) I also prefer not to have a space sent with each control code - so all 32's have been deleted by repoking where necessary.

This, of course, makes permanent the advice you gave to overcome start of paragraph indentation. However, it has to be remem- bered, and this applies to your advice as well,that right margin justification is upset.

3)I have to say that the problem of lack of right justification after the introduction of control codes is a fault, al- though I suspect to correct it would entail a great deal of work. In my experience only "The Last Word" was fault free in this respect and I feel it is a pity that 'OUTWRITE' doesn't measure up in this respect.

4)I found the lack of a flashing cursor annoying as I frequently managed to lose it.

However, your suggestion of a cure by use of a coloured cursor is brilliant. I introduced a red cursor and have had no problems at all since - incidentally I had no difficulty in following your instructions.

5) Now something of a 'tongue in cheek' comment. I think your criticism of Mike Haine's "delete" criticism is a litle unfortunate, as the program uses "delete" with two different meanings.

In the case of a symbol, it has the meaning replace "symbol" by "space" - but in the case of a line, "delete" means "remove line in its entirety" - and not "replace line by a line of spaces"! These usages may follow "usual custom" which is really the basis of your criticism of Mike Haine's comment, but repetition of 'common' error is no basis for valid criticism!

Now, a word on FREEWARE and P.D. SOFTWARE which has implication for programs like "OUTWRITE".

You have commented that extended programs offering facilities that only few might use could only be marketed at greatly increased, (uneconomic?) prices.

I suggest that the introduction of FREEWARE and P.D. SOFTWARE makes it necessary to grasp that particular nettle - since their introduction has gone too far to stop, even if it were wanted - and there is at least one prog- ram, for all practical purposes as good as "OUTWRITE" available as FREEWARE.

This can only mean that there are enough programmers 'out there' to supply reasonable programs just for the fun of it. It also implies that 'programs for sale' have to be the extensive programs requiring a team of programmers employed by a software house.

That further implies that those of us who wish to acquire such programs will have to pay an economic market price. This, of course, only applies to 'serious' programs.

'Games' i.e. the saleable ones, already require a team to produce them, but the market volume is sufficient to keep the price to a reasonable level.

The only other way would be for the software houses to subsidise the serious programs from the profits of the games programs c.f. the claims always made that "pop" records subsidise "classical".

After all the doom and gloom, may I offer you both a belated happy New Year - and keep up the good work. I am still amazed that you continue to further improve the magazine - I am unable to comprehend how you manage to do it.

Yours sincerely,

Frank Lambert

From: Alan D. Cox, Pen-y-Maes, Ostrey Hill, St.Clears, Dyfed, SA33 4AJ

Dear Ron and Brian,

First, at the risk of being a bore, may I again comment that I cannot see how SCPDSA can say they are dealing in PD software and at the same time claim copy- right in their material - it really is a nonsense.

I note that despite the opportunity offered by earlier correspondence, including a letter of mine, Mr. Stevens has not attempted to justify his erroneous description of the material he is selling.

I found ALPHAKEY a useful item, if only because it gives the items in alphabetical order.

However, I think it a pity that John McCabe did not give the 'full' codes for all the key- words etc: specifically, he ignores the fact that for some of the items i.e. those given on page 65 of the Technical Manual, the correct code is FFh followed by the appropriate number.  The full code for SCREEN$ is 255 76.

This can be easily seen by writing a small BASIC program and then PEEKing the area in which it is stored (at DPEEK &5AA0 + &4000 - not &8000 as stated in the Technical Manual)

I was interested to see RAND- SCRAPER - I remember this prog- ram from my Spectrum days, and I thought I had a copy but cannot find it - was it in an early OUTLET?. It has been extensively reworked for SAM and is well worth republishing.

In Stephen Wilson's SAMCLASS he equates Hertz to cycles in one place - it should surely be cycles per second (sorry, but I get more pedantic as I grow older!) Whilst on the point of old age, I hope you will forgive me for saying that some of your more exotic opening screens for items are, for my poor old eyes, very difficult to read - an example this month is 4 Square,

with blocked letters in italics and with a shadow - and no, it is not my screen, which is better than average in my opinion (I originally typed 'view', but thought the pun un- fortunate!). It is only a minor moan, but if no-one tells you, you won't know of our problems!

I was interested to see SHRINK, which appears to be a SAM version of the classic pseudo-AI program called ELIZA. If your readers are interested in this subject they may like to look at Mike James' article in the February 1992 issue of Computer Shopper, entitled 'All in the mind' - and there are related articles in earlier Shoppers.

Having raised the question of copyright earlier in this letter, I have a problem in this area myself.   One of my sins - I'm not going to tell you the others! - is that I occasionally dabble with my Wife's AMSTRAD PCW 8256, and I also read 8000+ (now called PCW PLUS).

In the November 1991 issue there was an interesting short Mallard BASIC program to print out bar- codes given an input of the bar- code number. Out of interest, and also because the author's name happened to be Alan Dennis (which are my Christian names) I decided to convert this to a SAM program (not difficult, but not trivial either.

I appreciated the Spectrum/SAM string-slicing commands more and more as I struggled with the Mallard equivalents).

Once this was working, I thought it might be of some interest to other Spectrum/SAM users, so I wrote to the Editor of 8000+ asking if she would object if my version was published in OUTLET (i.e. if you were interested).

However, 8000+ operate a policy of only replying to letters if they can do so in their letters columns (which may be a reason- able policy for general letters, although I believe they would please their readers more if they were more responsive in

this area - and yes, I remember your comments on reacting to readers queries, although I think you are wrong), but I felt a query such as mine deserved a reply by letter, particularly since I had said I would fully acknowledge their copyright. However, as you can deduce I have had no response.

So where do I stand? If you think the program is of any interest, would you be prepared to publish it, with full recognition of 8000+ and the original author's copyright?

Or do you feel that the refusal of 8000+ to respond must be taken as refusal of the right to copy?

(I should say that I have not altered the essential ideas in the program, although the Spectrum/SAM conversions are my own work).

As a light aside, I do not know how many of your readers are superstitious but I wonder how many of those who are know that the 13th of a month is more likely to be a Friday than any other day of the week? I came across this fact many years ago in Rouse Ball's Mathematical Recreations and Essays, and verified it by hand. It is an interesting exercise in calendar calculations to check it out on Spectrum/SAM - the key is to remember the 400 year calendar cycle.

For those who may be concerned, the relative proportions of different days of the week are only just biased in favour of Friday.

Apropos versions of BASIC. Over Christmas I had the opportunity to play with my younger Son's ATARI 520STFM. He uses it for word processing and games, and has never seriously tried the BASIC supplied with the machine. I did - and it's APPALLING!

Say what you will about Clive Sinclair, he provided a splendid BASIC (which of course has influenced SAM's BASIC as well). Indeed, it might be argued that as well as encouraging the

growth of the hobby computer scene with his succession of excellent and affordable machines. The user-friendly nature of ZX80/81 and Spectrum BASIC also made a major contribution. If I had had to struggle with ATARI BASIC early on I might well have become totally disillusioned.

I note what you say in response to my comments on SAMCo's News- disk. I didn't expect you to agree with me!

However, if what you say about SAMCo using the Newsdisk as a medium for publishing a dis- assembly of the SAM ROM is true then things becomes even more ludicrous.

I don't expect to find serious technical material such as this in the midst of what is being offered as a collection of playable demos (presumably mainly of games, in which I have no real interest), news (i.e. advertisements) of SAM related products and gossip.

I hope that I shall not be denied the opportunity to get a disassembly of SAM's ROM just because I refuse to pay for what ought to be free advertising material.

Incidentally, as I said, I wrote to Alan Miles on this matter, but as yet I have not received the courtesy of either an acknowledgement or a reply.

And please do not tell me about the problem of firms replying to letters - by and large firms need customers more than customers need firms, and even if the firm believes that the customer is not always right, they should at least respond to criticisms.

As I said earlier, whatever the costs, a sensible firm ought to budget for dealing with letters in order to keep serious customers happy.

Finally, I recently acquired, through the pages of Micro Computer Mart, a Tandy Colour Graphics Printer CGP 115, which is a super little machine.

I'd be grateful to learn whether any of your readers can help me with a couple of problems - one with the DIP switches and one with the CHR$(19) command. I am happy for you to publish my address in case anyone wants to write to me directly.

As ever, all best wishes, and congratulations on a super 'magazine'

Alan Dennis Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

I think SCPDSA's claim to copy- right referred to their first disc in response to being asked why they corrupted the directory to prevent people copying the files. I don't know what other claims to copyright they make or if they have changed their pos- tion because it is simply not clear whether their material IS genuinely in the public domain or not.

Not all of the material in their catalogue is marked as "PD" and nowhere is "PD" defined.There is no declaration that "public domain" means anyone can copy it or sell it for a nominal cost as on other computers.

Nor is any of the software that I have seen marked as public domain or "FREEWARE" as we do.

The catalogue's front cover has the sub-heading "The Complete Guide to Public Domain Software For the SAM Coupe" which is obviously not true since they do not include any OUTLET material.

All-in-all, my feeling is that the originators used the label "PD" without knowing what it really means but have just heard it and thought it a "trendy" expression to use.

Not all the material is in the public domain because I have asked individuals.

I agree that they should either declare all or part of the mat- erial genuinely in the public domain and announce that it may be freely copied or re-sold so long as only a modest charge is made to cover costs (this cost MAY include labour costs as is the general practice with PD libraries on other computers) or they should remove the term "PD" from their name.

Again,the rights of contributing authors is paramount. Anyone writing software and wishing it to be in the public domain MUST be reassured that it will be treated as such and is free to be copied by anyone and dispers- ed as widely as possible.

Regarding your comment on copy- right, I must say that it IS normal for an author to declare his work "in the public domain" and yet retain the copyright but this is a technicality and is really just to make clear who the author really is or perhaps simply to stop anyone blatantly taking a PD program, dressing it up, packaging it and promoting it as their own software.It does NOT mean the software must not be copied etc or that the author has any further control such as cancelling the PD status!

Note PD means both"software free of copy restrictions" AND the blanket term for LICENCEWARE, SHAREWARE etc. where copyright IS crucial.

Again, with PD, it is as if one retains the copyright but allows the public free licence to copy it. In any event, that is the way it is - even if it is hard to understand. What doesn't make sense is declaring something PD and then saying nobody must copy it and even protecting it from being copied! This is nonsense.

I remove bugs, correct spelling and grammar, I may even add improvements (I add a front title page if there isn't one).

Я думаю, что претензия SCPDSA на авторские права относилась к их первому диску в ответ на вопрос, почему они повредили каталог, чтобы помешать людям копировать файлы. Я не знаю, какие еще претензии на авторские права они выдвигают или изменили ли они свою позицию, потому что просто неясно, находятся ли их материалы подлинно в общественном достоянии или нет.

Далеко не все материалы в их каталоге помечены как «PD», и нигде нет определения, что такое «PD». Нет никакого заявления о том, что «public domain» означает, что любой желающий может свободно копировать эти программы или продавать их по номинальной стоимости, как это принято на других компьютерах.

И ни одна из программ, которые я видел, не помечена как public domain или «FREEWARE», как это делаем мы.

На обложке каталога красуется подзаголовок: «The Complete Guide to Public Domain Software For the SAM Coupe» («Полный путеводитель по Public Domain ПО для SAM Coupe»), что очевидным образом неправда, поскольку они не включили ни одного материала из OUTLET.

В общем и целом, у меня сложилось впечатление, что авторы каталога использовали ярлык «PD», толком не понимая, что он на самом деле значит, а просто услышали его и решили, что это «модное» словечко.

Далеко не все представленные там материалы являются общественным достоянием, в чём я лично убедился, расспросив некоторых авторов.

Я согласен, что им следует либо признать все или часть материалов подлинным public domain и объявить, что их можно свободно копировать или перепродавать, если взимается лишь скромная плата для покрытия расходов (в эти расходы МОЖЕТ входить оплата труда, как это принято в PD-библиотеках на других компьютерах), либо убрать термин «PD» из своего названия.

Опять же, права авторов-составителей имеют первостепенное значение. Любой человек, пишущий программы и желающий сделать их достоянием общественности, ДОЛЖЕН быть уверен, что с его трудом будут обращаться соответствующим образом, и что любой желающий волен копировать его и распространять как можно шире.

Что касается вашего комментария об авторских правах: должен сказать, что для автора ВПОЛНЕ нормально объявить свою работу «in the public domain» и при этом сохранить за собой copyright. Но это лишь формальность, служащая лишь для того, чтобы четко указать, кто является настоящим создателем, или просто помешать какому-нибудь наглецу взять PD-программу, приукрасить её, упаковать в красивую коробочку и продавать под видом своей собственной разработки. Это НИ В КОЕМ СЛУЧАЕ не означает запрета на копирование и т.д., и не дает автору права в дальнейшем отменять статус PD!

Заметьте: аббревиатура PD означает как «программы без ограничений на копирование», ТАК И выступает зонтичным термином для LICENCEWARE, SHAREWARE и т.п., где авторское право (copyright) ИМЕЕТ решающее значение.

Опять же, в случае с PD всё выглядит так, будто автор сохраняет за собой авторские права, но даёт общественности свободную лицензию на копирование. В любом случае, так уж повелось — даже если это трудно понять. А вот что действительно лишено всякого смысла, так это объявлять что-то PD, а затем утверждать, что никому нельзя это копировать, или вовсе ставить защиту от копирования! Вот это — чистейший нонсенс.
